title: The default bridge network
idea: The default bridge is the private network every container joins unless you pick another. Containers on it reach each other by IP address, not by name.

analogy.text: An apartment block with numbered flats and no name board. You can knock on a flat only if you know its number.
analogy.breaks: Every door is unlocked: any container can reach any other.

points: Without `--network`, `docker run` attaches the container to the `bridge` network.
Docker gives each container a private IP address on that network.
Containers on it reach each other by IP address; a name fails to resolve.
Outgoing connections use the host's IP address; incoming ones need a published port.

steps.caption: Start two containers with no `--network` flag. Both join the default `bridge` network.
Each box shows an example address. Docker hands them out from the bridge's private range.
`tool` calls `api` by IP address. The bridge passes the packet on, and it arrives.
`tool` calls `api` by name. The default bridge has no name lookup, so the call fails.
From outside the host, a container answers only on a published port, such as `-p 8080:3000`.
Outgoing connections need no flag. They leave through the host's own IP address.

code.caption: Two containers on the default bridge: reach one by IP address, then by name.

walk.text: Start the API with no `--network` flag. It joins the default `bridge`.
Start `tool` from `alpine`. `-dit` keeps it running in the background.
Inspect the default network. Its `Containers` section lists each container's IP address.
Call the API from `tool` by IP address: copy `api`'s address from the output. This works.
Call it by name. The name does not resolve, so the call fails.

pitfalls: Names fail on the default bridge; use a custom network (next page).
On Docker Desktop the host cannot reach a container's IP; publish a port.
Avoid the default bridge in production; Docker's docs recommend user-defined networks.

quiz.q: Two containers run on the default bridge. How can `tool` reach `api`?
quiz.why: The default bridge has no name lookup. `localhost` is the container itself, and a published port is for traffic from outside.

takeaway: On the default bridge, containers find each other only by IP address.

starters: How do I find a container's IP address?
